name: MonarchAiTypingDots
title: AiTypingDots
summary: Three dots that rise and brighten in turn to show the assistant is writing, for places with no room for a sentence.
whenToUse: In a chat dock, a list row or an empty assistant message bubble while the reply has not started to stream.
whenNotToUse: For other people typing in a conversation use MonarchTypingIndicator, which names them. For the progress of a task use MonarchProgress.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiTypingDots(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchAiTypingDotsSize = MonarchAiTypingDotsSize.Md, announce: Boolean = true, label: String? = null)

options.name: size
options.description: Sm: 4dp dots for docks and dense rows. Md: 6dp dots for a message bubble.

options.name: announce
options.description: Makes the dots a polite live region whose text is set one frame after they appear, so TalkBack announces them. Pass false when something else already announces the state.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "Assistant is typing" (monarch_aitypingdots_label).

states.name: animating
states.description: Each dot rises by 0.6 of its size and turns from the assistant border color to the strong assistant color, one after another, in a 1.2-second cycle.

states.name: animations off
states.description: The dots stand still in the strong assistant color.

appearance: Dots in the strong assistant color at the top of their rise and the assistant border color at rest, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The timing follows the web: a cycle of three quarters of the shimmer duration and an eighth of it between dots. The web fades the dots from 40% opacity; Android moves between two assistant color roles instead, because Monarch does not dim colors with alpha. The web keeps the label in visually hidden text; Android sets it as the content description of the one element. iOS names the flag isAnnounced; Android uses announce, as the web does.
accessibility: The dots are one TalkBack element whose content description is the label, "Assistant is typing" by default.
With announce the element is a polite live region and its text is set one frame after it appears, so the label is announced without moving focus.
With announce false the element has the label but no live region.
The dots do not move when the user has turned animations off.
The dots grow with the font size setting.
edgeCases: The label is announced each time the dots enter the composition; insert them once per reply, not per token.
A rising dot is drawn above the element's bounds by up to 0.6 of its size, inside the vertical padding the component keeps.

examples.title: Sizes
Small, in a dock that announces the state itself
